title: The fall of the Western Roman Empire
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:17Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers the fall of the Western Empire but never mentions Christianity or Christendom, which the new point's brief makes a central idea, so no existing card teaches the same thing.

draft.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
card: The Roman Empire was so large that it was later split into a western and an eastern half. The Western Roman Empire was ruled from Italy and covered lands such as Italy, Gaul (now France) and Spain.
In the 400s CE, the western half broke apart. Groups from outside the empire, such as the Goths and the Vandals, took over Roman lands and set up their own kingdoms.
The usual date given for the end of the Western Empire is 476 CE, when its last emperor was removed. The Eastern Roman Empire carried on for about another thousand years.
After Rome fell, there was no single ruler over western Europe. Christianity spread and became a shared faith across many kingdoms. Historians call the Christian lands of Europe Christendom.
draft.remember: The West broke into many kingdoms in the 400s CE, and a shared Christian faith joined much of Europe as Christendom.

a.q: What happened to western Europe after the Western Roman Empire broke apart?
opts: Many separate kingdoms formed under new rulers
One new empire replaced it under a single ruler
The Eastern Roman Empire ended at the same time
Each region was left with no rulers at all
a.why: Groups such as the Goths and Vandals set up their own kingdoms on Roman lands. There was no single ruler, but there were still rulers. The Eastern Empire kept going, so it did not end at the same time.
a.clue: Think about who took over Roman lands.

b.q: In 700 CE, a traveller moves between three kingdoms in western Europe. Each has its own king, yet people in all three worship in Christian churches. What does this show?
opts: Christianity joined many kingdoms as Christendom
The Western Roman Empire still ruled all three
The three kingdoms had one king in common
Christianity had ended the Eastern Roman Empire
b.why: With no single ruler after Rome, the shared Christian faith was one thing linking the kingdoms. Historians call this Christendom. The kings were separate, so the empire was not still in charge and the three did not share a king.
b.clue: The kings are separate. What do the people share?

a.best: Many separate kingdoms formed under new rulers

b.best: Christianity joined many kingdoms as Christendom
